festival.name: Atardecer Bachata Festival
festival.tagline: Sea by day, club by night.
festival.description: Three days of bachata in Valencia. Workshops on the sand and in a seaside pavilion by day, socials with DJs, live acts and shows in a club by night. Beginners are welcome, and the Dominican roots of the dance are part of the programme.

themes.theme: dancers from many countries in one city

ticket.notes: Price per person. Book four or more passes together.

option.title: By plane
option.text: Fly to Valencia Airport. The metro runs from the airport to the city in about 25 minutes. A taxi to the beachfront takes about 25 minutes.

option.title: By train
option.text: High-speed trains arrive at the main station in the city centre. From there, the tram or a bus goes to the beachfront.

option.title: Between venues
option.text: All three venues are within a 15-minute walk of each other along the beachfront. The festival provides a signed walking route.

option.title: By bike
option.text: Valencia has a long coastal cycle path. Bikes can be parked next to the Arena Stage and Pabellón Brisa.

entry.question: Which workshop level should I pick?
entry.answer: Pick beginner if you have danced bachata fewer than ten times. Pick intermediate if you can dance a full song with turns. Pick advanced if you dance often and want to refine technique. The Which level am I? quiz on the Programme page helps you decide.

entry.question: Do I need a partner?
entry.answer: No. Workshops rotate partners, and every workshop has a role focus of lead, follow or both. Socials are open to everyone.

entry.question: What does the Full Pass include?
entry.answer: The Full Pass includes all workshops, all socials, all shows and entry to all three venues for the whole festival.

entry.question: What should I wear?
entry.answer: Wear light clothes for the day. Bring shoes you can dance in. For the sand, many dancers dance barefoot or in socks. Nights are warm, and the club has a cloakroom.

entry.question: Are the venues step-free?
entry.answer: Yes. All three venues have step-free access. See the Accessibility page for details on each venue, including quiet rooms and accessible toilets.

entry.question: When do the night socials end?
entry.answer: Friday and Saturday club socials run until 06:00 or earlier. The Sunday farewell night ends around 02:30. Check each set on the Programme page.

entry.question: How do I report a problem?
entry.answer: Tell any staff member wearing a Atardecer T-shirt, or write to info@atardecer.example. All reports are handled in confidence. See the Code of conduct page.

entry.question: Can I transfer or cancel my pass?
entry.answer: You can transfer your pass to another person for free until 14 days before the festival. Cancellations are not refunded.

codeOfConduct.summary: Atardecer is a place to dance, and everyone has the right to feel safe, respected and free to say no.

principles.principle: Ask before you dance. A no is a complete answer, with or without a reason.
Respect your partner's boundaries on the dance floor, in dips and in close hold.
Leaders and followers are equal partners. Nobody has to dance with anyone.
No unwanted touching, comments or photos.
Look out for each other. Step in kindly if you see something wrong, or tell a staff member.
Respect all levels. Beginners are welcome, and teaching on the floor is for classes only unless asked.
Alcohol is not an excuse for crossing a boundary.

accessibility.summary: All three venues have step-free entrances, accessible toilets and a quiet space. This website is built to WCAG 2.0 AA.

features.feature: Step-free access to Arena Stage, Pabellón Brisa and Marea Club
Quiet rooms at the pavilion and the club
Free ear protection at the club bar
Contact us before the festival if you have specific needs

sustainability.summary: The festival is held on a public beach. We keep the sea and the sand clean and cut waste where we can.

commitments.commitment: Reusable cups at every bar, with a small deposit
Free refill points for drinking water at all three venues
A recycling station at each venue and a beach clean-up on Sunday morning
Signed walking and cycling routes so you do not need a car
No single-use plastic bottles on sale

roots.intro: Bachata began in the Dominican Republic and has become one of the most danced Latin styles in the world. It grew in the barrios of Santo Domingo, where guitar-led songs about love and daily life were played at small parties.

event.text: The first bachata recordings are made in the Dominican Republic. They are commonly dated to this year.
Bachata grows in rural and working-class neighbourhoods. Many people look down on the music, and it is rarely played on the radio.
Bachata becomes popular across the country. Guitar styles evolve, and the music reaches a wider audience.
Modern bachata spreads worldwide. Dancers start to dance it in a close hold, and the sensual style emerges in Europe.
UNESCO inscribes bachata dominicana on its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

instrument.name: Requinto guitar
instrument.text: A lead guitar that plays the melody lines and gives bachata its bright, twanging sound.

instrument.name: Segunda guitar
instrument.text: A rhythm guitar that supports the lead guitar.

instrument.name: Bongo
instrument.text: A pair of small drums that mark the steady pulse the dancers follow.

instrument.name: Güira
instrument.text: A metal scraper that gives the rhythm its fine, scratchy texture.

instrument.name: Bass
instrument.text: Plays a simple repeating line under the guitars.

type.label: Social
type.description: Open dancing with a DJ or live music.

level.label: Beginner
level.description: You know the basic step or are new to bachata. You can dance part of a song with a partner.

level.label: Intermediate
level.description: You can dance a full song with turns and you feel the music.

level.label: Advanced
level.description: You dance often, lead or follow with confidence and want to refine technique.

level.label: All levels
level.description: Open to everyone. Used for socials, shows and relaxed classes.

style.label: Bachata dominicana
style.description: The traditional Dominican style with lively footwork.

style.label: Bachata sensual
style.description: A close, flowing style with body movement.

style.label: Bachata moderna
style.description: A modern style that mixes turns, musicality and open and close hold.

dayPart.label: Night (Club)
dayPart.description: Sessions that start at 20:00 or later.

venue.name: Arena Stage
venue.description: A sand-floor stage on the beachfront. It hosts the daytime sand workshops, the sunset socials and the open-air shows.

accessibility.notes: A firm boardwalk leads from the promenade to the edge of the dance floor. The sand floor itself is soft.

venue.name: Pabellón Brisa
venue.description: An air-conditioned seaside pavilion with a sprung wooden floor. It hosts most workshops, the evening practica socials and the pavilion showcases.

accessibility.notes: Step-free entrance on the street side. A quiet room is open all day next to the main floor.

venue.name: Marea Club
venue.description: The indoor club for the main night socials. It has a large floor, a stage for live acts and two bars. Late sets run until the early morning.

programmeItem.title: Welcome Sea Social: DJ Kiko Mar
programmeItem.description: DJ Kiko Mar plays bachata dominicana on the sand. Dance by the sea.

programmeItem.title: Your first bachata: the basic step
programmeItem.description: Start from zero. Learn the basic step in four counts, the side step and how to pause between songs. No partner needed.

programmeItem.title: Salsa on the sand: cross-body for bachata dancers
programmeItem.description: A relaxed all-levels class that borrows the cross-body lead from salsa and shows how it fits a bachata song.

programmeItem.title: Follow with ease: connection basics
programmeItem.description: Learn how to read a lead through the frame and the hand, and how to stay relaxed in a slow song.

programmeItem.title: Bachata on sand: balance and footwork
programmeItem.description: Sand changes how you step. Learn to keep your weight low, keep your steps small and stay balanced barefoot or in shoes.

programmeItem.title: Lead with ease: clear signals for beginners
programmeItem.description: Learn three simple lead signals, how to count the room and how to ask a stranger to dance.

programmeItem.title: Follower styling in the sea breeze
programmeItem.description: Add arm styling and soft body waves without losing your connection. For followers who know the basic step well.

programmeItem.title: Turn patterns that flow
programmeItem.description: Link three turn patterns without stopping. You work on timing, spotting and a quiet frame.

programmeItem.title: Leading spins without pulling
programmeItem.description: Learn to prepare, signal and release a spin with the frame, not the arm.

programmeItem.title: Slow musicality: dancing the pauses
programmeItem.description: Use silence, breaks and slow tempos. Explore how to listen first and move second.

programmeItem.title: Sunset steps: Dominican footwork for everyone
programmeItem.description: A sunset class on the roots of the dance: the side step, the tap and the small hip movement of traditional bachata.

programmeItem.title: Practica Social: DJ Lorena Vela
programmeItem.description: DJ Lorena Vela plays bachata moderna in the pavilion. A relaxed floor where beginners are welcome to join.

programmeItem.title: Opening Show: Ola Brava Dance Company and Sal y Compás
programmeItem.description: Ola Brava Dance Company and Sal y Compás on stage, with live music by Cuarteto Salitre. A short show for everyone, standing room only.

programmeItem.title: Pavilion Showcase: Estudio Candela and Navío Dance Crew
programmeItem.description: Estudio Candela and Navío Dance Crew on stage, with live music by Los Faroleros del Puerto. A short show for everyone, standing room only.

programmeItem.title: Club Night: DJ Tarek Noor
programmeItem.description: DJ Tarek Noor plays bachata sensual in the club. The main floor for dancers who stay up late. With live music by Yeral Bonilla.

programmeItem.title: Midnight Show: Cuerpo & Mar and Raíz Viva Ensemble
programmeItem.description: Cuerpo & Mar and Raíz Viva Ensemble on stage, with live music by Trío Güira y Sal. A short show for everyone, standing room only.

programmeItem.description: DJ Ximena Flor plays bachata moderna in the club. The main floor for dancers who stay up late.

programmeItem.title: Last Dance Set: DJ Anouk Bell
programmeItem.description: DJ Anouk Bell plays bachata sensual in the club. The main floor for dancers who stay up late.

programmeItem.title: Morning basics by the sea
programmeItem.description: A relaxed first class on the sand with the basic step and the side step. Bring water and sunscreen.

programmeItem.title: Saturday starter: the follower's basics
programmeItem.description: Learn the basic step, how to follow weight changes and how to stay light on your feet. Good first class for followers.
